full_judgment:
II. That the appellate Court being final court of facts committed an error of law, resulting in erroneous decision, occasioning failure of justice in decreeing the suit without considering the evidence on record and without rebutting the findings arrived at by the trial Court on consideration of exhibit 'Kha' of the defendants, the pattan in favour of their predecessor in the year 1945. Korfa pattan and the C.S, S.A. and R.S. record, rent receipt and also the decrees declaring the title of the defendants to the suit land, and as such the judgment of the High Court Division in revision making the Rule absolute suffers from no legal infirmity and calls for no interference by this Division. 

 10. The trial Court observed that the decree in Other Class Suit No.140 of 1974 is not binding of the plaintiffs since they or their predecessor were not party to that suit and similarly in Other Class Suit No.282 of 1976 neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessor were party and hence the decree is not binding upon the plaintiffs. It was further observed that defendant No. 1 having claimed that he took pattan of the suit land, could not produce the original amalnama or dakhila and did not give any satisfactory explanation. As a result the claim of defendant Nos.5/6 regarding the alleged pattan is not believable. However, the trial Court then went on to consider that the mutation khatian and rent receipts are evidence to prove their possession. It is noted that the trial Court took into account the submission of the learned Advocate for the plaintiffs that defendant No.5 who deposed as D.W. I admitted that he was the Nayeb in the Tahsil Office and that the submission of the learned Advocate for the plaintiffs that he had created false and forged pattan and obtained mutation and rent receipts in his name with a view to grab the land, was not without basis. Upon considering the evidence of the witnesses and the materials on record, the trial Court concluded that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land and although defendant Nos.5/6 produced mutation khatian and rent receipts, there is good reason to suspect that those are collusive. However, the trial Court dismissed the suit of the plaintiffs on the finding that the korfa title of the plaintiffs' predecessor subsisted, but they were unable to produce any evidence to prove such title. 

 15. The appellate Court further noted that the trial Court found possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs and also noted that the defendants' claimed that defendant No.1 took pattan of the suit land, but were unable to produce the original amalnama/pattannama/dakhila and were unable to give any satisfactory explanation. The appellate Court as the last court of fact found that the claim of pattan as made by defendant Nos.5/6 was not believable.
